No new hot symbol above 1.2 percent that is not ordinary steady-state work. The two new columns are not visible in the profile at all. THE REAL FINDING IS THE THRESHOLD. CENSUS_ALARM_SECS is 900.0 (cli/tests/suite/census_duration.rs:133). Over the twelve most recent recorded censuses the band is 855.5 to 979.5 with a MEDIAN of 902.8 -- so the alarm sits at the 42nd percentile of its own noise band and 7 of 12 healthy runs trip it. The median run is ABOVE the alarm. An alarm that fires on the majority of healthy runs is not detecting anything; it is a coin flip that bills a human for a written justification each time, which is exactly how the yellow log accumulated a NOT FLAMEGRAPHED row that rolled its obligation forward twice. The Escapement already established that the plus-or-minus 7 percent wall spread is parallel-efficiency scheduling rather than work -- wall and CPU-s are visibly decoupled across the band -- so the variance the alarm keeps catching is known, characterised and not a defect. HONEST LIMITATION: call-graph stitching under --call-graph fp on this optimized build was poor, so I did NOT reproduce The Escapements 82.80 percent cumulative figure for runner::build_row and am not asserting a cumulative breakdown. The self-time comparison is the evidence, and it is a like-for-like comparison against the same command on the same box. RECOMMENDATION: move the threshold above the measured band (or key it on cpu_ratio, which separates contention from regression) rather than continuing to pay a forced look per coin flip.
